Your fury has unlocked a primal connection to the Force, granting you the ability to cast force powers (see chapter 10 for general forcecasting rules and chapter 11 for the force powers list).

Force Powers Known. You start knowing 4 force powers of your choice, learning more as you gain levels, per the Force Powers Known column of the Marauder Approach Forcecasting table. You can't learn a power above your current Max Power Level, though you may learn a power at the same time you learn whatever it requires as a prerequisite.

Force Points. You have a pool of force points, spent to cast your powers, equal to your berserker level (per the Force Points column of the Marauder Approach Forcecasting table) plus your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice). This pool refills completely after a long rest.

Max Power Level. Some force powers can be overpowered for a stronger effect at the cost of more force points; the highest level you can overpower a power to rises as you level, per the Max Power Level column of the Marauder Approach Forcecasting table. You may cast a power at 4th level only once between long rests, regaining that ability after finishing one.

Forcecasting Ability. Which ability governs your powers depends on their alignment: Wisdom for light-side powers, Charisma for dark-side powers, and either (your choice) for universal powers. This is the ability you use whenever a power calls for your forcecasting ability, including for setting a power's save DC and for its attack rolls.

Force save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your forcecasting ability modifier

Force attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your forcecasting ability modifier
